after.name: External Agent submits a model patch

claim.explanation: run accepts --patch for validate/diff/apply; load_json rejects malformed JSON and duplicate keys before dispatch into preview/apply. apply also requires --expected-revision.

validate --patch and diff --patch both call preview: read and validate current model, build a candidate, calculate impact and append a candidate revision in memory. The response reports committed:false; no save or lock is performed.
The external Agent inspects affected objects/scenarios and may submit apply in a separate invocation. Preview does not reserve its revision, and review/retry policy belongs to the caller.
assumptions: An external Agent chooses whether to apply after reviewing preview output.

claim.explanation: apply delegates to commit with a candidate-builder callback. Under the file lock (30-second timeout), commit rereads and validates the saved model before comparing expected_revision.
A revision mismatch raises REVISION_CONFLICT before invoking the builder or writing. main returns ok:false and exit 1; the caller must reread and reconcile before resubmission.

The builder parses Patch, copies current model data, derives maintenance observations and processes operations sequentially. Facts are append-only, IDs cannot change, create cannot overwrite reserved IDs, and update/delete require existing objects. Update fields replace whole values. Complete-model validation checks references, hierarchy and evidence. revision_candidate preserves binding history, derives impact, increments revision, appends author/summary/timestamp/affected IDs and validates again.

Still holding the lock, commit prepares the committed:true result and atomic_write serializes the candidate into a temporary file beside the model, flushes and fsyncs, then os.replace publishes it. os.replace is the commit point; finally removes a remaining temporary file.

ModelError or caught IO/lock errors become ok:false JSON and exit 1 if output delivery succeeds. LOCK_TIMEOUT and pre-replace validation/save failures do not commit this patch. Errors after os.replace or output delivery require reading the model to establish outcome.
After commit returns, main writes and flushes ok:true JSON with committed:true, revision and diff, then exits 0 if delivery succeeds.

If JSON stdout write/flush raises OSError or UnicodeError, main attempts an stderr diagnostic and returns 2. This does not roll back os.replace; an observed delivery failure alone does not establish whether apply committed.

A separate read invocation returns the complete validated saved model when no scope is supplied. Inspect revision and explanation before retrying after conflict or uncertain delivery; read itself does not retry apply.

transitions.condition: validate/diff with a successfully loaded patch
apply with successfully loaded patch and required expected revision
Argument or patch JSON load failure caught by main
Preview succeeds and its JSON is delivered; no persistent mutation
External Agent elects a separate apply invocation using the reviewed patch and read revision; this is not an internal call
Saved revision differs from expected revision
Lock acquired, read succeeds, saved revision equals expected revision
Lock timeout or read failure before builder
Caller elects to inspect current model before rebuilding a patch
All operation, evidence, history and model validation succeeds
Candidate construction or validation raises; saved model remains unchanged
Save completes and commit returns its prepared result
Save raises; before os.replace no commit, after it inspect model rather than assuming rollback
stdout write/flush fails after successful commit return
Error JSON stdout write/flush also fails
Caller performs a separate read to determine actual persisted state

claim.explanation: Source-backed explanation of the optional external preview/review loop and transactional apply boundary. Component reuse reflects shared responsibilities with read-to-html. Conditional transitions summarize nested calls and caller actions; display order is not an execution trace.
assumptions: The external Agent authors a patch against a complete read; user intent and semantic correctness are not validated by this subsystem.
Filesystem supports the file lock and same-directory os.replace used by the implementation.
issues: Agent decision/reconciliation is outside Python source and is marked inference; no internal provider or automatic retry exists.
The filelock implementation, filesystem durability guarantees and browser JS are outside this Python-only snapshot.
Structural validation is not proof of the submitted business explanation; exceptional stderr failure can prevent the intended exit-2 diagnostic.
